label: r3c3
name: half-roll, 4x updates, lr 2e-3
hypothesis: Same as r2c1, but lr goes from 0.001 to 0.002. With only about 120 updates and training success still rising at the end, a bigger step size should get further within the budget. PPO clipping and gradient clipping should limit instability. Refuted if dev success falls below about 0.86, or one seed collapses, which would mean the bottleneck is update count rather than step size.
last_analysis: The observed target is shifted by X//2 columns. Adding a half-rolled copy of the observation fixed this: the score went from 0 to 0.59. After that, the recipe mattered most. Refreshing data more often at the same number of gradient steps (128→64 envs, 128 samples per minibatch) raised dev success from 0.82 to 0.885, and lr 2e-3 raised it to 0.913 (best; both seeds about 0.90 or higher). Going further failed. Rollout_len 8 collapsed (0.076), probably from heavy bootstrapping and tiny advantage batches. Two epochs with 128 envs lost one seed (0.90 vs 0.15). The global broadcast gave no clear gain (0.874 vs 0.885). At the end of training, training success (0.90) roughly equals dev success, so the limit is how fast the agent learns, not generalisation or capacity. A bigger network would cost samples and updates. For this last round I keep the best architecture and change one optimisation setting per candidate: a higher lr, 3 PPO epochs (about 30% more fresh samples and updates), and a lower entropy bonus so the greedy policy sharpens sooner.
